title: Configure HTTP/3 connection budgets without preview scaffolding
goal: Set per-connection HTTP/3 stream and buffer budgets, preserve backpressure, and remove preview acknowledgements only on a framework that no longer requires them.

selectionNotes: All four properties already exist on .NET 10 with RequiresPreviewFeatures. Retain its narrowly scoped CA2252 acknowledgement; .NET 11 needs neither that acknowledgement nor EnablePreviewFeatures.
Stream limits apply per connection, not per user/process or to application request quotas. Leave at least the HTTP/3 control/QPACK stream credit required by the protocol.
Read/write thresholds provide transport backpressure, not exact process-memory, request-body-size or end-to-end byte limits. Native/protocol/client buffers also participate.

Windows x64 only is executed here. The fixture requires native MsQuic 2.5.11.159415436, uses a private self-signed certificate without installing trust, and fails rather than silently falling back to HTTP/2.

evidence.scope: Real Windows x64 Kestrel HTTP/3: two concurrent requests and queued third on one connection, three inbound unidirectional protocol streams and cancelled fourth open, slow 16MiB upload/download pause and resume. Actual MsQuic module/version/hash, audited references, compiler and runtime hashes. No exact memory/quota/other-OS/GA claim.
